# Put document-period dates in chronological order

## Project interpretation
When both boundaries of the document period are present, the end cannot precede
the start. This check concerns ordering; it does not decide which service dates
the transaction should use.

## Common causes
- Start and end fields were swapped during mapping.
- A date range crossed a month boundary and the month was copied incorrectly.
- Locale-specific input was parsed with the wrong day and month order.

## Safe fix
Return to the source period, correct the mapped dates, and serialize them as ISO
dates. Do not reverse values automatically without confirming their meaning. The
fixture is corrected to end after it starts, then the complete document is
revalidated.

## Failing fragment
```xml
<cac:InvoicePeriod>
  <cbc:StartDate>2026-07-15</cbc:StartDate>
  <cbc:EndDate>2026-07-01</cbc:EndDate>
</cac:InvoicePeriod>
```

## Corrected fragment
```xml
<cac:InvoicePeriod>
  <cbc:StartDate>2026-07-15</cbc:StartDate>
  <cbc:EndDate>2026-07-31</cbc:EndDate>
</cac:InvoicePeriod>
```
